images.name: tax-season-day
images.title: A March Tuesday at an *accounting firm*
rows: A client uploads a W-2 from two years back. It spots the wrong year and asks for the right one.
Sends second reminders to 14 clients still missing documents, each with their own list.
Answers six "is my return done?" emails from the practice management software.
A client forwards an IRS letter. It files it and sends it to the assigned accountant.
Categorizes March transactions for three bookkeeping clients and lists the questions it has.
A client asks whether they should amend last year's return. It books a call with their accountant.
A client asks to split their invoice into two payments. It writes up the request for a partner.

images.name: setup
images.title: How it *is set up* at a firm
steps: Add the AI Employee as a user and vendor in the firm's written information security plan.
Map a season of client email
Sort last spring's messages by type: documents, status, scheduling, billing, advice.
What each client usually sends, built from last year's file.
Portal, practice management and client books. No e-filing, no moving money.
Returns, advice, notices, fee changes and upset clients go to a named person.
It drafts every message and categorization while someone reads each one.
Update it when forms, deadlines, banks or clients change.
